newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes higher in quiet trade.

text.p: * Forex traders mostly out, attending conference
The Philippine peso closed slightly higher at 26.275 to the dollar from yesterday's 26.279 in quiet, range-bound trading, traders said.
"Most of the players are in the Asia Pacific conference ... Even the Central Bank has only two traders on deck," one trader said. Central Bank has been the major player in the market.
Most of the traders were attending the two-day 18th Asia Pacific Forex Assembly at a Manila hotel.
Value turnover was thin at $88.5 million as compared with yesterday's $137.90 million.

Banks were selling dollars in anticipation to buy them back on Friday on arbitrage play. Banks buying dollars on Friday have until Monday to settle their trade. Banks have two days over the weekend to hold on to their pesos and earn higher interest.
The Central Bank did not intervene in the market keeping its bid-offer quote at 26.235/26.285 and later to 26.23/26.28.
Demand from oil companies was minimal at $2.5 million.
